description.text: The promos of the Black & White Series, numbered BW01 to BW101 and released from March 2011 to December 2013, when the prefix changed from HGSS to BW. Most came in products: blisters of each expansion, tins, boxes and collections. Some went to players, from prerelease events, which also gave staff copies, to the World Championships trophy cards Tropical Beach (2011 and 2012) and Champions Festival (2013); the Supporter N, BW100, was a Pokémon League prize. Keldeo and Genesect came with DVD releases of their films. Two numbers were never released: Pikachu BW77 and Raichu BW78 were meant for the Plasma Freeze three-pack blisters of May 2013, but after a planned English Landorus Box was cancelled, Landorus BW79 and Druddigon BW80 went into the blisters instead. Pokémon.com showed the two cards for one night in July 2014, and they could be played in the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online, but no printed copy was ever sold.

Ken Sugimori's drawing first came in Japan in September 2010 in the Journey Partners collection, with Snivy standing in front of a house; the English card puts it on a new swirling background. Japan reprinted its own version several times, last as a prize of JR Hokkaido's Pokémon Battle Train in August 2011, for finishing the Reshiram Route on the games' Battle Subway. The English art came back in 2021 with the 25th anniversary logo, in McDonald's collection that year and as a jumbo card in the Unova First Partner Pack.

description.text: Champions Festival was the promo card of the 2013 Pokémon World Championships, the first card of that name, given out at the tournament held from 9 to 11 August 2013 at the Vancouver Convention Centre, the first World Championships outside the United States. Competitors received the card in seven languages, staff got a Staff copy, and the top finishers in each division got copies stamped with their placement, from Top Thirty-Two up to Champion. How many trophy copies were handed out changed from year to year.

description.text:
A holofoil Eevee from the Legendary Treasures three-pack blister of November 2013, with three Legendary Treasures booster packs and a coin. The other three-pack blister held Mew BW98. These blisters' promos were the first printed on a smoother style of cosmos holofoil, which replaced the earlier pixel-style pattern until 2023.

Akira Komayama's art, with Eevee in front of Pikachu, first came in Japan as Eevee 235/BW-P, the prize of a stamp rally at 7-Eleven stores for the Pokémon Fair 2013. Players who collected four different stamps of 24 at different stores received it, with stamps of Pokémon from that year's film from 15 to 31 July and of Legendary and Mythical Pokémon from 1 to 15 August.

description.text:
A Genesect from the Red Genesect Collection of 25 September 2013, released ahead of the English film Genesect and the Legend Awakened. The collection held a 60-card deck built around the shiny red Genesect, a Red Genesect pin, a metallic Genesect coin, a deck box, damage counters, a playmat and two Black & White Series booster packs. The same card with other art, BW101, came with the film's DVD in December 2013.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan on 13 July 2013 as Genesect 231/BW-P, in the EX Battle Boost Campaign Pack, a blister of four EX Battle Boost booster packs released with that set, a Mewtwo vs Genesect deck kit and the film's Japanese premiere.
